checks: No eclipse at 1 of 5 covered epochs where the 5.02069 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 156780644 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 5.020692 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 22.08% dimming, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal strength is high, with a BLS detection significance of 448.0 and pixel-level confirmation showing a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 66.2. However, an important caveat applies: the odd and even eclipses differ significantly in depth, which indicates the true orbital period is twice the initial measurement. The target does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel candidate. The pixel-level analysis detected the source 3.5 arcsec from the target location, and the machine-learning screening score of 0.20 suggests moderate confidence in this being a genuine stellar target.
